title: Family-specific machine learning prioritizes enzyme variants for prospective testing
summary: Researchers screened 1,513 natural SGNH-hydrolase homologues and trained task-specific sequence CNNs on the resulting activity, thermostability, and substrate-preference data. The models helped select candidates for a prospective 230-sequence assay panel, where CNN-selected candidates were enriched for target traits relative to generalist pretrained and physics-based baselines; the panel also included other selection strategies and random controls. Assays used clarified E. coli lysates and measured relative maximum velocity, integrating expression and catalysis. The first public version with this result was posted to bioRxiv on 2026-06-03; a Research Square version followed on 2026-06-05.
ai_technology: Task-specific convolutional neural networks trained on amino-acid sequences; CNN-based HEV and UCB selection strategies

evidence.tested: A prospective panel of 230 previously untested sequences was assayed; CNN selection strategies were enriched for the predicted target traits compared with generalist pretrained and physics-based approaches. The panel pooled sequences selected by multiple strategies and included random controls.
evidence.unknown: Clarified lysate MaxV integrates enzyme expression and catalytic activity and is not a purified-enzyme turnover measurement. The result is scoped to this enzyme family and the reported assay setup; prospective panel composition was mixed across selection strategies.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised family-specific CNNs trained on sequence and assay data ranked untested homologues for activity, thermostability, and substrate preference, and guided candidate selection for prospective experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text as indexed, including title, posting date, affiliations, methods, prospective assay results and limitations; primary Research Square v1 identity/date record.
